questions.stem: In the replicate pH measurement exercise below, a student records the following data. In the Mohr method for chloride determination, what signal marks the endpoint?

options.text: A color change of an organic metallochromic indicator
options.misconception: confuses the Mohr method with complexometric titration

options.text: A sharp drop in measured pH at neutrality
options.misconception: mistakes precipitation titration for acid-base titration

options.text: The disappearance of a red precipitate of silver chloride
options.misconception: misstates the color and direction of the change

options.text: Formation of a brick-red silver chromate precipitate once chloride has been consumed

questions.explanation: In the Mohr method chromate indicator remains soluble while chloride is present, because silver chloride precipitates first. Once chloride is used up, excess silver precipitates chromate as a brick-red solid. It is not a metallochromic indicator or a pH endpoint.
questions.hint: Think about which silver salt precipitates last.
